verses.text: Then the men and their wives began to complain loudly against their fellow Jews.
Some said, "We have many sons and daughters. We need grain so we can eat and stay alive."
Others said, "We are giving up our fields, vineyards, and houses as security for loans so we can get grain during the famine."
Others said, "We had to borrow money to pay the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

We are the same as our fellow Jews, and our children are just as good as theirs. But we have to sell our sons and daughters as slaves. Some of our daughters have already been made slaves. We can do nothing about it, because our fields and vineyards now belong to other people."
When I heard their complaints and what they said, I was very angry.
I thought it over, and then I accused the important men and the officials. I told them, "You are charging your own relatives interest!" So I called a large meeting to deal with them.

I said to them, "As much as we could, we have bought back our fellow Jews who were sold to foreigners. Now you are selling your own relatives, so that they will have to be sold back to us!" They were silent and could not find anything to say.
I went on, "What you are doing is not right. You should live in the fear of our God, so our enemies among the nations will have no reason to insult us.
My relatives, my servants, and I are also lending the people money and grain. Please, let's stop charging interest!
Give back to them today their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses. Also give back the interest you are charging them, the one percent on the money, grain, new wine, and olive oil."

They answered, "We will give it back, and we will not ask them for anything more. We will do as you say." Then I called the priests and made the leaders promise in front of them to do what they had said.

I also shook out the folds of my robe and said, "In the same way, may God shake out of their house and property anyone who does not keep this promise. May that person be shaken out and left with nothing!" The whole crowd said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did what they had promised.

From the time I was made governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years in all, my relatives and I did not eat the food the governor was allowed.

The governors before me had put heavy loads on the people. They took food and wine from them, plus about half a kilogram of silver. Even their helpers ruled over the people harshly. But I did not act like that, because I feared God.
I also worked hard on the wall. We did not buy any land, and all my men gathered there to work.
At my table I fed one hundred fifty Jews and officials, besides the people who came to us from the nations around us.

Every day one ox, six of the best sheep, and some birds were prepared for me. Every ten days a large supply of all kinds of wine was brought. Even so, I did not ask for the food the governor was allowed, because the people already had heavy burdens.
Remember me kindly, my God, for all the good I have done for these people.
